title: Magic Dice
body:
Goal: make a dice roller with pick random and two variables. Time: about 10 minutes. Tool: Scratch app (offline).

Build steps

  1. Open Scratch. Make two variables: roll and rolls (For all sprites).
  2. Build the two scripts below. join and pick random are in Operators. Type a space after "You rolled" so the words don't squash together.
  3. Click the green flag, then press space to roll.
  4. Roll 10 times and write the numbers in your homework sheet.
  5. Save as magic-dice.

The scripts in words

  1. when green flag clicked
    • set rolls to 0
    • say "Press space to roll!"
  2. when space key pressed
    • set roll to (pick random 1 to 6)
    • change rolls by 1
    • say (join "You rolled " (roll))
    • if roll = 6 then
      • start sound (any)

Expected behavior

After the green flag, rolls shows 0 and the sprite says "Press space to roll!". Each time you press space, the sprite says a number from 1 to 6, like "You rolled 4", and rolls goes up by 1. Rolling a 6 also plays a sound. You can never predict the next number.

Checklist

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Make two variables first: roll and rolls. One holds the number you just rolled. The other counts how many times you rolled. You need two scripts: one for the flag and one for the space key.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: Use pick random (Operators category) to choose the number and store it in roll. Use the join block (Operators category) to glue words and the roll variable together inside a say block. Use an if block for the sound.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: The space script starts with set roll to (pick random ____ to ____). Next, change rolls by a small number. Then say (join "____ " (____)). Last, an if block that checks whether roll is the lucky number, with a start sound inside. Remember the space after the words.
